title: Spatially-Resolved Plasmon EELS for Determining Thermal Properties and Phase Transitions
content: The thermal properties of materials, including the thermal expansion coefficient, melting point, and temperature-dependent phase transitions, can differ significantly at the nanoscale from their bulk values due to confinement or surface effects. Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), with the ability to probe the material properties with sub-Å spatial resolution,[1] can be an essential tool to exploring these properties at the nanometer scale or below. By combining HR-STEM imaging with EELS experiments during in-situ heating or cooling experiments, the response of a material to external stimuli can now be probed in the temperature range between 20 – 1,300 K while maintaining atomic resolution. [2-3] In this contribution, we will explore STEM-based techniques, including plasmon-EELS imaging, to determine properties, such as thermal expansion, melting and solidification, and structural phase changes, as the result of sample temperature. [4-5]
